---
title: "Parquet conversion scaling"
output:
  github_document:
    html_preview: false
    pandoc_args: ["--wrap=preserve", "--columns=400"]
---

This report gives the 1×/2×/4× scaling evidence `STYLE.md` asks for, for the
COPY statements that the `*_convert_parquet_sql` builders return. Issue
https://github.com/RGenomicsETL/duckhts/issues/298 lists these executed COPY
workloads for BAM, VCF and GFF as not measured. A builder only returns SQL;
the caller executes it, as the R wrappers do through DBI. Here each
observation builds the statement, untimed, and executes it in a fresh DuckDB
CLI process. No earlier report measures these workloads; this is their first
baseline.

## Workloads

Every input is a registry artifact of `r/duckhtsbench`. Before anything is
measured, each is checked against the identity the registry records: its
checksum and size, or its counted content. The ONT alignment records neither,
so the report gives its SHA-256. The builders run with their defaults, plus
the region or column list that cuts the input and, for the CRAM, the
reference.

- **BAM, short reads** (`duckhts_bam_convert_parquet_sql`, which reads SAM,
  BAM and CRAM): the chr1 CRAM slice of the 1000 Genomes 30× sample HG00403
  (`bam_mismatch_hg00403_chr1_cram`, 150-base reads), with the registered
  GRCh38 FASTA as the reference (`liftover_grch38_fasta`). The 1×, 2× and 4×
  regions start at the beginning of chr1 and end at the 12.5%, 25% and 50%
  quantiles of the alignment start positions, so each holds twice the
  alignments of the one before.
- **BAM, long reads**: the minimap2 alignment of an ONT E. coli K-12 run
  (`ont_ecoli_k12_bam`). Its regions end at the 25% and 50% quantiles of the
  mapped start positions and at the end of the chromosome. The whole file has
  fewer reads than one row group holds, so this series measures wide rows
  that never fill a row group. Its runs take well under 5 s, so it gets a
  memory verdict only.
- **VCF, records** (`duckhts_bcf_convert_parquet_sql`): the GIAB HG002 v4.2.1
  phased benchmark VCF on GRCh38 (`geno_giab_phased_source`, indexed by
  `geno_giab_phased_source_tbi`), one sample on chr1 to chr22. The 1× and 2×
  regions list the chromosomes in header order up to the record at the 25%
  and 50% rank; the 4× region lists all of them.
- **VCF, samples**: the 1000 Genomes phase 3 chr22 cut of the SQL scaling
  audit (`sql_scaling_phase3_1x`, biallelic SNVs of 2,504 samples). Its records
  are fixed. `columns :=` keeps the record columns and the GT columns of the
  first 626, 1,252 and 2,504 samples in header order. In the builders' layout
  every sample is one column, so the samples set the width of a row.
- **GFF** (`duckhts_gff_convert_parquet_sql`): the GENCODE v49 basic
  annotation (`gencode_v49_basic_gff3`). The 1× input is the file itself; the
  2× and 4× inputs are two and four copies of it, concatenated at render time.
  Each copy is a whole gzip member, and the reader decompresses the members in
  sequence.

The cuts, the concatenated copies and the input denominators (rows and
decoded bytes) are computed at render time, untimed. Those passes read every
input in full, so every measured run reads from a warm page cache.

## Observations

Every observation is one fresh DuckDB CLI process under `/usr/bin/time`, which
gives the peak RSS. The JSON profiler gives the latency of the COPY statement,
its CPU time, the time of the reader and of the COPY operator, and DuckDB's
peak buffer and temporary bytes. `max_temp_directory_size` is zero, so a spill
fails the render; the memory limit is DuckDB's default, which the report
records. Each run writes its output into a temporary directory and deletes it
once its size, rows, row groups and DuckHTS metadata are read. The render
stops if less than 10 GiB is free on that file system before a run. Each cell
has three repetitions at one thread and at four threads, run in an order that
alternates sizes. The render command pins the processes to four cores and
runs them at scheduling priority −15. The builder query that returns the
statement is run before each observation and is not timed; it reads only the
header.

## Budget, declared before measuring

The overhead is the median peak RSS of three empty runs that start the CLI,
load the extension and run no COPY.

The ceiling of each observation is overhead + 3 × the live state below, and it
is a gate: the render stops if any observation exceeds its ceiling or spills.
The live state follows the reader contracts and the Parquet writer of DuckDB
v1.5.1 (`7dbb2e646f`, the CLI used here):

- **One writer.** The generated COPY keeps insertion order, and DuckHTS's
  table functions, registered through the C API, report no batch index:
  `src/execution/operator/scan/physical_table_scan.cpp:255` needs
  `get_partition_data`, which `src/main/capi/table_function-c.cpp` never sets.
  `ParquetWriteExecutionMode` then picks `REGULAR_COPY_TO_FILE`
  (`extension/parquet/parquet_extension.cpp:661-668`), whose sink is not
  parallel
  (`src/include/duckdb/execution/operator/persistent/physical_copy_to_file.hpp:88-89`).
  One thread scans and buffers, whatever the `threads` setting.
- **The row group.** The sink buffers decoded rows until it holds
  `row_group_size` rows, 100,000 by default in the builders, and checks this
  after each chunk of 2,048 rows (`parquet_extension.cpp:371-390`). A byte limit
  applies only when `ROW_GROUP_SIZE_BYTES` is given, and DuckDB refuses that
  option while insertion order is kept (`parquet_extension.cpp:333-337`). So a
  row group holds R = min(rows, 102,047) rows of w bytes. w is the decoded
  width of a row in DuckDB's vector layout: 16 bytes for each string plus its
  bytes beyond 12, 16 bytes for each list plus its elements, and the fixed
  width of every other value. Validity bits, under 1%, are left out. w is
  counted from each input before measuring.
- **Its encoded pages.** Each page is compressed into a buffer of ZSTD's bound
  of its plain-encoded size (`extension/parquet/column_writer.cpp:156-163`), and
  the writer keeps all of them until the row group is written
  (`extension/parquet/parquet_writer.cpp:512-599` and `637-690`). Plain encoding
  is never larger than the decoded layout for these column types, so this is
  at most R × w. The uncompressed buffers of the pages being encoded are freed
  page by page; the factor of 3 covers them.
- **Column dictionaries.** The state of each leaf column holds a dictionary of
  NextPowerOfTwo(2 × ⌊R/5⌋) slots of at most 24 bytes and a target buffer of at
  most 1 MiB until the row group is written
  (`extension/parquet/include/writer/templated_column_writer.hpp:66-75`,
  `src/include/duckdb/common/primitive_dictionary.hpp:37-62`): at most 2.5 MiB
  per column when R is 102,047.
- **The reader.** One output chunk of 2,048 rows, 2,048 × w bytes, and the
  state of htslib 1.24 (`third_party/htslib`):
  - for a CRAM read with the builders' default of two decompression threads,
    htslib shares one copy of the reference between the threads and loads the
    whole contig (`cram/cram_io.c:3253` and `5573-5585`): 248,956,422 bytes for
    chr1. It decodes slices ahead into a queue of twice the threads and reads
    one slice past it (`cram/cram_decode.c:3517-3523`), so up to 7 slices of at
    most 10,000 alignments (`cram/cram_structs.h:87`) are held. For each
    decoded alignment, with its name, bases, qualities and tags, 1 KiB is
    allowed;
  - for BAM, VCF and GFF, 8 MiB is allowed for the file buffers (64 KiB BGZF or
    gzip blocks, and at most twice the threads in queued decompression jobs:
    `bgzf.c:1756-1758`), the header and one record.

That is 2 × R × w + leaf columns × the dictionary + 2,048 × w + the htslib
state.

The render also stops if any output's row count differs from its input's or
lacks the DuckHTS reader metadata. For every series whose 1× run takes at
least 5 s on one thread, which is the least that `STYLE.md` accepts for a
timing verdict, it stops if a time exponent is above 1.25 at either doubling.
A series under 5 s gets the memory verdict alone.

``` sh
nice -n -15 taskset -c 16-19 Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("benchmarks/benchmark_convert_parquet_scaling.Rmd")'
```

`CONVERT_PARQUET_BENCH_SIZE=reduced` runs the same code on small inputs, to
check the report end to end: CRAM regions of 0.2% to 0.8% of the alignments,
VCF regions of 1/64 to 1/16 of the records, 8 to 32 samples, and copies of
the MANE annotation (`mane_v15_ensembl_gff3`) instead of GENCODE. That run
writes its observations to a temporary directory, so pass `output_dir` to keep
its report out of `benchmarks/` too; its numbers are not evidence.

``` sh
CONVERT_PARQUET_BENCH_SIZE=reduced taskset -c 0-3 Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("benchmarks/benchmark_convert_parquet_scaling.Rmd", output_dir = "/tmp")'
```

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

```{r benchmark, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
stopifnot(requireNamespace("duckhtsbench", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE))
Sys.setenv(DUCKHTSBENCH_REGISTRY = normalizePath(
  "r/duckhtsbench/inst/benchmark_registry.tsv", mustWork = TRUE))
extension <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("DUCKHTS_EXTENSION", "build/release/duckhts.duckdb_extension"),
                           mustWork = TRUE)
duckdb_cli <- Sys.getenv("DUCKDB_CLI", Sys.which("duckdb"))
stopifnot(nzchar(duckdb_cli), file.exists("/usr/bin/time"))
duckdb_runtime <- system2(duckdb_cli, "--version", stdout = TRUE)[[1L]]
revision <- system2("git", c("rev-parse", "HEAD"), stdout = TRUE)
src_tree <- system2("git", c("rev-parse", "HEAD:src"), stdout = TRUE)
if (system2("git", c("diff", "--quiet", "HEAD", "--", "src"), stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE) != 0L) {
  stop("Build source must match the recorded HEAD")
}
host_load <- sub(".*load average: ", "", system2("uptime", stdout = TRUE))
quote_literal <- function(value) paste0("'", gsub("'", "''", value, fixed = TRUE), "'")
quote_ident <- function(value) paste0('"', gsub('"', '""', value, fixed = TRUE), '"')

# The sizes: the full workloads described above, or small inputs that check
# the report end to end and write their observations outside benchmarks/.
bench_size <- Sys.getenv("CONVERT_PARQUET_BENCH_SIZE", "full")
if (!bench_size %in% c("full", "reduced")) {
  stop("CONVERT_PARQUET_BENCH_SIZE must be full or reduced", call. = FALSE)
}
full_size <- identical(bench_size, "full")
cram_fractions <- if (full_size) c(0.125, 0.25, 0.5) else c(0.002, 0.004, 0.008)
giab_fractions <- if (full_size) c(0.25, 0.5, 1) else c(1, 2, 4) / 64
sample_counts <- if (full_size) c(626L, 1252L, 2504L) else c(8L, 16L, 32L)
gff_id <- if (full_size) "gencode_v49_basic_gff3" else "mane_v15_ensembl_gff3"
runs_csv <- if (full_size) "benchmarks/benchmark_convert_parquet_scaling_runs.csv" else
  file.path(tempdir(), "benchmark_convert_parquet_scaling_runs.csv")
reduced_note <- if (full_size) "" else paste(
  "**Reduced sizes.** This render ran with `CONVERT_PARQUET_BENCH_SIZE=reduced`: its inputs are smaller",
  "than the workloads above describe, its observations were written to a temporary directory, and its",
  "numbers are not evidence.")

# One untimed statement in its own CLI process; its rows come back as a data frame.
query_untimed <- function(sql) {
  output <- system2(duckdb_cli, c("-unsigned", "-csv", "-bail"),
                    input = c(sprintf("LOAD %s;", quote_literal(extension)), sql), stdout = TRUE)
  status <- attr(output, "status")
  if (!is.null(status) && status != 0L) stop("untimed query failed (status ", status, ")", call. = FALSE)
  utils::read.csv(text = output, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
}
memory_limit <- query_untimed("SELECT current_setting('memory_limit') AS memory_limit;")$memory_limit

# The temporary file system takes every output and the concatenated copies.
disk_floor_bytes <- 10 * 2^30
free_bytes <- function(path) {
  report <- system2("df", c("-Pk", shQuote(path)), stdout = TRUE)
  1024 * as.numeric(strsplit(trimws(report[[length(report)]]), "[[:space:]]+")[[1L]][[4L]])
}
check_free_space <- function() {
  if (free_bytes(tempdir()) < disk_floor_bytes) {
    stop("less than 10 GiB free on the temporary file system", call. = FALSE)
  }
}
check_free_space()

# Registry inputs, each checked against the identity the registry records.
artifact <- function(id) {
  path <- duckhtsbench::duckhts_bench_artifact_path(id)
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("registry artifact ", id, " is not staged: ", path, call. = FALSE)
  duckhtsbench::duckhts_bench_validate_identity(id, path)
  path
}
registered <- function(id) {
  registry <- duckhtsbench::duckhts_bench_registry()
  duckhtsbench:::duckhts_bench_identity_fields(registry$supplier_identity[match(id, registry$id)])
}
cram <- artifact("bam_mismatch_hg00403_chr1_cram")
reference <- artifact("liftover_grch38_fasta")
ont_bam <- artifact("ont_ecoli_k12_bam")
giab_vcf <- artifact("geno_giab_phased_source")
stopifnot(identical(artifact("geno_giab_phased_source_tbi"), paste0(giab_vcf, ".tbi")))
phase3_vcf <- artifact("sql_scaling_phase3_1x")
gff_source <- artifact(gff_id)
# The ONT alignment registers no checksum; its digest identifies the file read here.
ont_sha256 <- strsplit(system2("sha256sum", shQuote(ont_bam), stdout = TRUE), " ", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]][[1L]]

# CRAM: the registered content identity and the start-position quantiles, in one pass.
cram_fields <- registered("bam_mismatch_hg00403_chr1_cram")
cram_scan <- query_untimed(sprintf(paste(
  "SELECT count(*) AS alignments, sum(POS)::BIGINT AS position_sum, sum(len(SEQ))::BIGINT AS base_sum,",
  "quantile_disc(POS, %s) AS q1, quantile_disc(POS, %s) AS q2, quantile_disc(POS, %s) AS q4",
  "FROM read_bam(%s, reference := %s);"), format(cram_fractions[[1L]], scientific = FALSE),
  format(cram_fractions[[2L]], scientific = FALSE), format(cram_fractions[[3L]], scientific = FALSE),
  quote_literal(cram), quote_literal(reference)))
stopifnot(cram_scan$alignments == as.numeric(cram_fields[["alignments"]]),
          cram_scan$position_sum == as.numeric(cram_fields[["position_sum"]]),
          cram_scan$base_sum == as.numeric(cram_fields[["base_sum"]]),
          cram_scan$base_sum == 150 * cram_scan$alignments)
cram_regions <- sprintf("chr1:1-%s", format(c(cram_scan$q1, cram_scan$q2, cram_scan$q4), scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE))
# htslib loads the whole contig named by the regions, and holds up to seven slices.
reference_index <- utils::read.delim(paste0(reference, ".fai"), header = FALSE)
chr1_length <- reference_index[[2L]][reference_index[[1L]] == "chr1"]
cram_slices <- length(readLines(gzfile(paste0(cram, ".crai"))))
stopifnot(length(chr1_length) == 1L, cram_scan$alignments / cram_slices <= 10000)
cram_htslib_bytes <- chr1_length + 7 * 10000 * 1024
other_htslib_bytes <- 8 * 2^20

# ONT: one contig; quantiles of the mapped start positions.
ont_contig <- query_untimed(sprintf(
  "SELECT id, length FROM read_hts_header(%s) WHERE record_type = 'SQ' ORDER BY idx;", quote_literal(ont_bam)))
stopifnot(nrow(ont_contig) == 1L)
ont_scan <- query_untimed(sprintf(paste(
  "SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM read_bam(%s)) AS reads, count(*) AS mapped,",
  "quantile_disc(POS, 0.25) AS q1, quantile_disc(POS, 0.5) AS q2 FROM read_bam(%s) WHERE RNAME = %s;"),
  quote_literal(ont_bam), quote_literal(ont_bam), quote_literal(ont_contig$id)))
ont_regions <- sprintf("%s:1-%s", ont_contig$id,
                       format(c(ont_scan$q1, ont_scan$q2, ont_contig$length), scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE))

# GIAB: the record at each cut rank in header order of contig, then position.
# A cut of the whole file lists every contig instead.
giab_contigs <- query_untimed(sprintf(paste(
  "WITH contigs AS (SELECT id AS chrom, idx FROM read_hts_header(%s) WHERE record_type = 'contig')",
  "SELECT c.chrom, c.idx, count(*) AS records FROM read_bcf(%s) r JOIN contigs c ON c.chrom = r.CHROM",
  "GROUP BY c.chrom, c.idx ORDER BY c.idx;"), quote_literal(giab_vcf), quote_literal(giab_vcf)))
stopifnot(identical(giab_contigs$chrom, paste0("chr", 1:22)))
giab_ranks <- ceiling(sum(giab_contigs$records) * giab_fractions[giab_fractions < 1])
giab_cuts <- query_untimed(sprintf(paste(
  "WITH contigs AS (SELECT id AS chrom, idx FROM read_hts_header(%s) WHERE record_type = 'contig'),",
  "ranked AS (SELECT c.idx, r.CHROM AS chrom, r.POS AS pos, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY c.idx, r.POS) AS k",
  "FROM read_bcf(%s) r JOIN contigs c ON c.chrom = r.CHROM)",
  "SELECT k, idx, chrom, pos FROM ranked WHERE k IN (%s) ORDER BY k;"),
  quote_literal(giab_vcf), quote_literal(giab_vcf), paste(format(giab_ranks, scientific = FALSE), collapse = ", ")))
stopifnot(nrow(giab_cuts) == length(giab_ranks))
giab_region <- function(cut) {
  whole <- giab_contigs$chrom[giab_contigs$idx < cut$idx]
  paste(c(whole, sprintf("%s:1-%s", cut$chrom, format(cut$pos, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE))), collapse = ",")
}
giab_regions <- c(vapply(seq_len(nrow(giab_cuts)), function(i) giab_region(giab_cuts[i, ]), character(1L)),
                  if (any(giab_fractions == 1)) paste(giab_contigs$chrom, collapse = ","))
stopifnot(length(giab_regions) == 3L)

# Phase 3: the record columns and the GT columns of the first samples in header order.
phase3_columns <- query_untimed(sprintf(
  "SELECT column_name FROM (DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM read_bcf(%s));", quote_literal(phase3_vcf)))$column_name
sample_columns <- phase3_columns[startsWith(phase3_columns, "FORMAT_")]
record_columns <- phase3_columns[!startsWith(phase3_columns, "FORMAT_")]
stopifnot(length(sample_columns) == 2504L, all(startsWith(sample_columns, "FORMAT_GT_")))
columns_argument <- function(samples) {
  sprintf("columns := [%s]", paste(quote_literal(c(record_columns, sample_columns[seq_len(samples)])), collapse = ", "))
}

# GFF: the file itself, and two and four copies of it as consecutive gzip members.
staging <- tempfile("convert-parquet-inputs-")
dir.create(staging)
gff_copies <- c(1L, 2L, 4L)
gff_paths <- vapply(gff_copies, function(copies) {
  if (copies == 1L) return(gff_source)
  path <- file.path(staging, sprintf("%dcopies-%s", copies, basename(gff_source)))
  stopifnot(file.copy(gff_source, path))
  for (copy in seq_len(copies - 1L)) stopifnot(file.append(path, gff_source))
  stopifnot(file.size(path) == copies * file.size(gff_source))
  path
}, character(1L))

cells <- rbind(
  data.frame(series = "bam_short_reads", macro = "duckhts_bam_convert_parquet_sql", scale = c(1L, 2L, 4L),
             path = cram, input = cram_regions, samples = NA_integer_, htslib_bytes = cram_htslib_bytes,
             arguments = sprintf("region := %s, reference := %s", quote_literal(cram_regions), quote_literal(reference)),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  data.frame(series = "bam_long_reads", macro = "duckhts_bam_convert_parquet_sql", scale = c(1L, 2L, 4L),
             path = ont_bam, input = ont_regions, samples = NA_integer_, htslib_bytes = other_htslib_bytes,
             arguments = sprintf("region := %s", quote_literal(ont_regions)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  data.frame(series = "vcf_records", macro = "duckhts_bcf_convert_parquet_sql", scale = c(1L, 2L, 4L),
             path = giab_vcf, input = giab_regions, samples = 1L, htslib_bytes = other_htslib_bytes,
             arguments = sprintf("region := %s", quote_literal(giab_regions)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  data.frame(series = "vcf_samples", macro = "duckhts_bcf_convert_parquet_sql", scale = c(1L, 2L, 4L),
             path = phase3_vcf, input = sprintf("%s samples", format(sample_counts, big.mark = ",")),
             samples = sample_counts, htslib_bytes = other_htslib_bytes,
             arguments = vapply(sample_counts, columns_argument, character(1L)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  data.frame(series = "gff_records", macro = "duckhts_gff_convert_parquet_sql", scale = c(1L, 2L, 4L),
             path = gff_paths, input = sprintf("%d %s", gff_copies, ifelse(gff_copies == 1L, "copy", "copies")),
             samples = NA_integer_, htslib_bytes = other_htslib_bytes, arguments = "", stringsAsFactors = FALSE))

# The COPY statement the builder returns for one cell and output path.
build_copy_sql <- function(cell, output) {
  call <- sprintf("SELECT %s(%s, %s%s);", cell$macro, quote_literal(cell$path), quote_literal(output),
                  if (nzchar(cell$arguments)) paste0(", ", cell$arguments) else "")
  statement <- system2(duckdb_cli, c("-unsigned", "-list", "-noheader", "-bail"),
                       input = c(sprintf("LOAD %s;", quote_literal(extension)), call), stdout = TRUE)
  stopifnot(is.null(attr(statement, "status")), length(statement) == 1L, startsWith(statement, "COPY ("))
  statement
}
# The SELECT inside a generated COPY statement: what the measured run reads.
copy_select <- function(statement, output) {
  parts <- strsplit(statement, paste0(") TO ", quote_literal(output), " ("), fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  stopifnot(length(parts) == 2L)
  substring(parts[[1L]], nchar("COPY (") + 1L)
}

# Decoded width in DuckDB's vector layout: fixed widths, 16 bytes per string
# or list, string bytes beyond the 12 that are stored inline, list elements.
fixed_width <- c(BOOLEAN = 1, TINYINT = 1, UTINYINT = 1, SMALLINT = 2, USMALLINT = 2, INTEGER = 4,
                 UINTEGER = 4, FLOAT = 4, BIGINT = 8, UBIGINT = 8, DOUBLE = 8)
heap_bytes_sql <- function(value) sprintf("CASE WHEN strlen(%s) > 12 THEN strlen(%s) ELSE 0 END", value, value)
variable_bytes_sql <- function(column, type) {
  if (type == "VARCHAR") return(heap_bytes_sql(column))
  if (type == "VARCHAR[]") {
    return(sprintf("coalesce(len(%s), 0) * 16 + coalesce(list_sum(list_transform(%s, lambda x: %s)), 0)",
                   column, column, heap_bytes_sql("x")))
  }
  element <- sub("[]", "", type, fixed = TRUE)
  if (endsWith(type, "[]") && element %in% names(fixed_width)) {
    return(sprintf("coalesce(len(%s), 0) * %d", column, fixed_width[[element]]))
  }
  stop("no decoded width for column type ", type, call. = FALSE)
}
# Rows and decoded bytes of the SELECT that a cell's COPY reads. The COPY is
# not run here; the output path only completes the builder call.
count_input <- function(cell) {
  output <- file.path(staging, "denominator.parquet")
  select_sql <- copy_select(build_copy_sql(cell, output), output)
  schema <- query_untimed(sprintf("SELECT column_name, column_type FROM (DESCRIBE %s);", select_sql))
  fixed <- schema$column_type %in% names(fixed_width)
  variable <- schema[!fixed, , drop = FALSE]
  sums <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(variable)), function(i) {
    sprintf("sum(%s)::BIGINT AS v%d", variable_bytes_sql(quote_ident(variable$column_name[[i]]),
                                                         variable$column_type[[i]]), i)
  }, character(1L))
  counted <- query_untimed(sprintf("SELECT count(*) AS rows, %s FROM (%s);", paste(sums, collapse = ", "), select_sql))
  row_bytes <- sum(fixed_width[schema$column_type[fixed]]) + 16 * nrow(variable)
  data.frame(rows = counted$rows, decoded_bytes = counted$rows * row_bytes + sum(unlist(counted[-1L])),
             leaf_columns = nrow(schema))
}
cells <- cbind(cells, do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(cells)), function(k) count_input(cells[k, ]))))
phase3_records <- unique(cells$rows[cells$series == "vcf_samples"])
stopifnot(length(phase3_records) == 1L, phase3_records == as.numeric(registered("sql_scaling_phase3_1x")[["records"]]),
          all(cells$rows[cells$series == "gff_records"] == gff_copies * cells$rows[cells$series == "gff_records"][[1L]]))

# One empty run: start the CLI, load the extension, run no COPY. Returns the
# peak RSS in KiB.
run_empty <- function() {
  scratch <- tempfile("convert-parquet-empty-")
  dir.create(scratch)
  on.exit(unlink(scratch, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  sql_path <- file.path(scratch, "query.sql")
  time_path <- file.path(scratch, "time.tsv")
  writeLines(c("SET threads = 1;", "SET max_temp_directory_size = '0KiB';",
               sprintf("LOAD %s;", quote_literal(extension)), "SELECT 1;"), sql_path)
  status <- system2("/usr/bin/time", c("-f", shQuote("%M"), "-o", shQuote(time_path),
                                       shQuote(duckdb_cli), "-unsigned", "-batch", "-bail"),
                    stdin = sql_path, stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE)
  if (status != 0L) stop("DuckDB CLI failed (status ", status, ")")
  as.numeric(readLines(time_path)[[1L]])
}
# The operators of a JSON profile tree, one row each.
profile_operators <- function(node) {
  own <- if (is.null(node$operator_type)) NULL else
    data.frame(type = node$operator_type, name = node$operator_name, seconds = node$operator_timing,
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  do.call(rbind, c(list(own), lapply(node$children, profile_operators)))
}
# Run one generated COPY in a fresh CLI process with the given threads and
# spill forbidden. The output is read, untimed, and deleted with its directory.
run_copy <- function(cell, threads) {
  scratch <- tempfile("convert-parquet-run-")
  dir.create(scratch)
  on.exit(unlink(scratch, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  output <- file.path(scratch, "output.parquet")
  sql_path <- file.path(scratch, "query.sql")
  profile_path <- file.path(scratch, "profile.json")
  time_path <- file.path(scratch, "time.tsv")
  statement <- build_copy_sql(cell, output)
  writeLines(c(
    sprintf("SET threads = %d;", threads),
    "SET max_temp_directory_size = '0KiB';",
    sprintf("LOAD %s;", quote_literal(extension)),
    "PRAGMA enable_profiling = 'json';",
    sprintf("PRAGMA profiling_output = %s;", quote_literal(profile_path)),
    paste0(statement, ";"),
    "PRAGMA disable_profiling;"
  ), sql_path)
  check_free_space()
  status <- system2("/usr/bin/time", c("-f", shQuote("%M\t%e"), "-o", shQuote(time_path),
                                       shQuote(duckdb_cli), "-unsigned", "-batch", "-bail"),
                    stdin = sql_path, stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE)
  if (status != 0L) stop("DuckDB CLI failed (status ", status, ") for ", cell$series, " ", cell$scale, "x")
  profile <- jsonlite::fromJSON(profile_path, simplifyVector = FALSE)
  operators <- profile_operators(profile)
  copy_operator <- operators[operators$type %in% c("COPY_TO_FILE", "BATCH_COPY_TO_FILE"), ]
  scan_operator <- operators[operators$type == "TABLE_SCAN", ]
  stopifnot(nrow(copy_operator) == 1L, nrow(scan_operator) == 1L)
  timing <- utils::read.delim(time_path, header = FALSE, col.names = c("max_rss_kib", "process_seconds"))
  written <- query_untimed(sprintf(paste(
    "SELECT m.num_rows AS output_rows, m.num_row_groups AS row_groups,",
    "(SELECT count(*) FROM parquet_kv_metadata(%s) WHERE decode(key) = 'duckhts_reader') AS reader_metadata",
    "FROM parquet_file_metadata(%s) m;"), quote_literal(output), quote_literal(output)))
  data.frame(seconds = as.numeric(profile$latency), cpu_seconds = as.numeric(profile$cpu_time),
             scan_seconds = scan_operator$seconds, copy_seconds = copy_operator$seconds,
             copy_operator = copy_operator$name, max_rss_kib = timing$max_rss_kib[[1L]],
             peak_buffer_bytes = as.numeric(profile$system_peak_buffer_memory),
             peak_temp_bytes = as.numeric(profile$system_peak_temp_dir_size),
             output_bytes = file.size(output), written, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

empty_runs <- vapply(seq_len(3L), function(run) run_empty(), numeric(1L))
overhead_mib <- median(empty_runs) / 1024
# Ceilings in MiB: overhead + 3 x the live state declared above.
row_group_size <- 100000
vector_size <- 2048
cells$width <- cells$decoded_bytes / cells$rows
cells$row_group_rows <- pmin(cells$rows, row_group_size + vector_size - 1)
dictionary_bytes <- function(rows) 2^ceiling(log2(pmax(2 * floor(rows / 5), 1))) * 24 + 2^20
cells$live_state_bytes <- 2 * cells$row_group_rows * cells$width +
  cells$leaf_columns * dictionary_bytes(cells$row_group_rows) + vector_size * cells$width + cells$htslib_bytes
cells$budget_mib <- overhead_mib + 3 * cells$live_state_bytes / 2^20

series_names <- unique(cells$series)
observations <- list()
for (repetition in 1:3) {
  order <- if (repetition %% 2L == 1L) c(1L, 2L, 4L) else c(4L, 2L, 1L)
  for (threads in c(1L, 4L)) {
    for (series in series_names) {
      for (scale in order) {
        cell <- cells[cells$series == series & cells$scale == scale, ]
        observed <- run_copy(cell, threads)
        observations[[length(observations) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
          series = series, scale = scale, threads = threads, repetition = repetition,
          rows = cell$rows, samples = cell$samples, decoded_bytes = cell$decoded_bytes,
          budget_mib = cell$budget_mib, observed, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      }
    }
  }
}
runs <- do.call(rbind, observations)
unlink(staging, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(runs, runs_csv, row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(runs$peak_temp_bytes == 0), all(runs$output_rows == runs$rows), all(runs$reader_metadata == 1))
over_budget <- runs[runs$max_rss_kib / 1024 > runs$budget_mib, ]
if (nrow(over_budget)) {
  print(over_budget[c("series", "scale", "threads", "repetition", "max_rss_kib", "budget_mib")])
  stop("observations exceed their declared memory budget", call. = FALSE)
}

groups <- split(runs, list(runs$series, runs$scale, runs$threads), drop = TRUE)
summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(groups, function(cell) {
  stopifnot(length(unique(cell$output_rows)) == 1L, length(unique(cell$row_groups)) == 1L)
  data.frame(series = cell$series[[1L]], scale = cell$scale[[1L]], threads = cell$threads[[1L]],
             rows = cell$rows[[1L]], row_groups = cell$row_groups[[1L]],
             output_mib = round(median(cell$output_bytes) / 2^20, 1),
             median_seconds = median(cell$seconds), min_seconds = min(cell$seconds), max_seconds = max(cell$seconds),
             scan_share = round(median(cell$scan_seconds / cell$seconds), 2),
             cpu_per_second = round(median(cell$cpu_seconds / cell$seconds), 2),
             median_rss_mib = round(median(cell$max_rss_kib) / 1024, 1),
             max_rss_mib = round(max(cell$max_rss_kib) / 1024, 1),
             max_buffer_mib = round(max(cell$peak_buffer_bytes) / 2^20, 1),
             budget_mib = round(cell$budget_mib[[1L]], 1), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
summary <- summary[order(match(summary$series, series_names), summary$threads, summary$scale), ]
rownames(summary) <- NULL

# Growth of the median time against the dimension the series doubles: the
# input rows, or the samples of the samples series. An exponent of 1 is linear.
exponents <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(summary, list(summary$series, summary$threads), drop = TRUE), function(s) {
  s <- s[order(s$scale), ]
  dimension <- if (s$series[[1L]] == "vcf_samples") sample_counts else s$rows
  growth <- function(low, high) log(s$median_seconds[[high]] / s$median_seconds[[low]]) / log(dimension[[high]] / dimension[[low]])
  data.frame(series = s$series[[1L]], threads = s$threads[[1L]], one_x_seconds = s$median_seconds[[1L]],
             ratio_2x = dimension[[2L]] / dimension[[1L]], ratio_4x = dimension[[3L]] / dimension[[2L]],
             time_exponent_2x = growth(1L, 2L), time_exponent_4x = growth(2L, 3L),
             rss_ratio_2x = s$median_rss_mib[[2L]] / s$median_rss_mib[[1L]],
             rss_ratio_4x = s$median_rss_mib[[3L]] / s$median_rss_mib[[1L]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
exponents <- exponents[order(match(exponents$series, series_names), exponents$threads), ]
rownames(exponents) <- NULL
one_thread_one_x <- exponents[exponents$threads == 1L, c("series", "one_x_seconds")]
timed_series <- one_thread_one_x$series[one_thread_one_x$one_x_seconds >= 5]
timed <- exponents[exponents$series %in% timed_series, ]
if (any(timed$time_exponent_2x > 1.25 | timed$time_exponent_4x > 1.25)) {
  print(timed)
  stop("a time exponent is above 1.25", call. = FALSE)
}
```

`r reduced_note`

Source revision: `r revision`; `src` tree `r src_tree`. DuckDB runtime: `r duckdb_runtime` (CLI). Extension SHA-256: `r strsplit(system2("sha256sum", extension, stdout = TRUE), " ", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]][[1L]]`. Host load at start: `r host_load`. DuckDB memory limit: `r memory_limit` (the default); temporary directory limit: 0. Every observation is in [`benchmark_convert_parquet_scaling_runs.csv`](benchmark_convert_parquet_scaling_runs.csv).

Overhead: `r round(overhead_mib, 1)` MiB.

## Inputs

The CRAM slice has `r format(cram_scan$alignments, big.mark = ",")` alignments in `r format(cram_slices, big.mark = ",")` slices; the ONT file has `r format(ont_scan$reads, big.mark = ",")` reads, `r format(ont_scan$mapped, big.mark = ",")` of them mapped, and SHA-256 `r ont_sha256`. `rows` are the rows each builder's SELECT returns, counted untimed; `decoded_mib` and `bytes_per_row` are their decoded size; `row_group_rows` is R, `leaf_columns` the columns of the output, and `live_state_mib` and `budget_mib` follow from the model above.

```{r inputs, echo=FALSE}
inputs <- cells[c("series", "scale", "input", "rows", "leaf_columns")]
inputs$decoded_mib <- round(cells$decoded_bytes / 2^20, 1)
inputs$bytes_per_row <- round(cells$width, 1)
inputs$row_group_rows <- cells$row_group_rows
inputs$live_state_mib <- round(cells$live_state_bytes / 2^20, 1)
inputs$budget_mib <- round(cells$budget_mib, 1)
knitr::kable(inputs, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Measurements

`seconds` are the latency of the COPY statement over three repetitions. `scan_share` is the share of it spent in the reader, the rest being the Parquet writer. `cpu_per_second` is DuckDB's CPU time per second of latency; htslib's decompression threads are not in it. `row_groups` and `output_mib` describe the Parquet file.

```{r summary, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(summary, digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Growth of the median time against the input rows, or against the samples of the `vcf_samples` series (an exponent of 1 is linear), the size ratio at each doubling, and peak-RSS ratios to 1×:

```{r exponents, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(exponents, digits = 3)
```

## Findings

```{r findings, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
cell_of <- function(series, scale, threads = 1L) {
  found <- summary[summary$series == series & summary$scale == scale & summary$threads == threads, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(found) == 1L)
  found
}
one_writer <- all(runs$copy_operator == "COPY_TO_FILE")
stopifnot(one_writer)
thread_ratio <- merge(summary[summary$threads == 1L, c("series", "scale", "median_seconds")],
                      summary[summary$threads == 4L, c("series", "scale", "median_seconds")],
                      by = c("series", "scale"), suffixes = c("_one", "_four"))
thread_ratio <- thread_ratio$median_seconds_four / thread_ratio$median_seconds_one
records_series <- c("bam_short_reads", "vcf_records", "gff_records")
flat <- exponents[exponents$series %in% records_series & exponents$threads == 1L, ]
samples_low <- cell_of("vcf_samples", 1L)
samples_high <- cell_of("vcf_samples", 4L)
mib_per_sample <- (samples_high$median_rss_mib - samples_low$median_rss_mib) / (sample_counts[[3L]] - sample_counts[[1L]])
untimed <- setdiff(series_names, timed_series)
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "Every observation is within its ceiling, none spills, and every output has its input's rows and the",
  "DuckHTS reader metadata; the render enforces all of this. Every COPY ran as one `COPY_TO_FILE`",
  "operator, the writer that keeps insertion order without batch indexes. DuckDB's CPU time is at most",
  "%.2f s per second of latency in any run, and four threads change the median time of a cell by a factor",
  "of %.2f to %.2f, so one DuckDB thread does the work whatever the setting.\n\n"),
  max(runs$cpu_seconds / runs$seconds), min(thread_ratio), max(thread_ratio)))
model_fit <- merge(summary[summary$threads == 1L, c("series", "scale", "median_rss_mib")],
                   data.frame(series = cells$series, scale = cells$scale, live_mib = cells$live_state_bytes / 2^20),
                   by = c("series", "scale"))
model_fit$share <- (model_fit$median_rss_mib - overhead_mib) / model_fit$live_mib
lowest <- model_fit[which.min(model_fit$share), ]
highest <- model_fit[which.max(model_fit$share), ]
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "On one thread the peak RSS above the overhead is between %.2f (`%s` at %d×) and %.2f (`%s` at %d×)",
  "times the declared live state, against the factor of 3 that the ceiling allows.\n\n"),
  lowest$share, lowest$series, lowest$scale, highest$share, highest$series, highest$scale))
rss_growth <- function(series) cell_of(series, 4L)$median_rss_mib - cell_of(series, 1L)$median_rss_mib
buffer_spread <- max(vapply(records_series, function(series) {
  diff(range(summary$max_buffer_mib[summary$series == series & summary$threads == 1L]))
}, numeric(1L)))
# Every input of these series fills a row group at the full sizes, not at the reduced ones.
rows_fill_row_group <- all(cells$rows[cells$series %in% records_series] >= row_group_size + vector_size - 1)
model_growth <- if (rows_fill_row_group) "the model holds no state that grows with the input" else
  "the model's live state grows only until an input fills one row group"
unexplained <- if (!rows_fill_row_group) "" else paste0(
  "; the model does not account for that change",
  if (buffer_spread <= 1) ", and it is not memory that DuckDB's buffer manager holds" else "")
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "In the three records series the writer flushes a row group at 100,000 rows, so %s, and DuckDB's peak",
  "buffer differs by at most %.1f MiB between the sizes of a series. From 1× to 4× on one thread the peak",
  "RSS changes by %+.1f MiB (a ratio of %s) for the CRAM, %+.1f MiB (%s) for the VCF and %+.1f MiB (%s)",
  "for the GFF%s.\n\n"),
  model_growth, buffer_spread,
  rss_growth("bam_short_reads"), format(round(flat$rss_ratio_4x[flat$series == "bam_short_reads"], 2), nsmall = 2),
  rss_growth("vcf_records"), format(round(flat$rss_ratio_4x[flat$series == "vcf_records"], 2), nsmall = 2),
  rss_growth("gff_records"), format(round(flat$rss_ratio_4x[flat$series == "gff_records"], 2), nsmall = 2),
  unexplained))
timed_sentence <- if (length(timed_series)) {
  sprintf("The time exponents of the series with a timing verdict (%s) are at most %.2f.",
          paste(sprintf("`%s`", timed_series), collapse = ", "),
          max(c(timed$time_exponent_2x, timed$time_exponent_4x)))
} else {
  "No series has a timing verdict at these sizes."
}
untimed_sentence <- if (length(untimed)) {
  sprintf(" %s %s less than 5 s at 1× and %s no timing verdict.",
          paste(sprintf("`%s`", untimed), collapse = ", "),
          if (length(untimed) == 1L) "takes" else "take",
          if (length(untimed) == 1L) "gets" else "get")
} else {
  ""
}
cat(timed_sentence, untimed_sentence, "\n\n", sep = "")
short4 <- cell_of("bam_short_reads", 4L)
vcf4 <- cell_of("vcf_records", 4L)
gff4 <- cell_of("gff_records", 4L)
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "On one thread, %s CRAM alignments convert in %.1f s (%s alignments per second, %.0f%% of the time in",
  "the reader) at %s MiB peak RSS; the model attributes %s MiB of that to the chr1 reference, which",
  "htslib loads whole for its decompression threads. %s VCF records take %.1f s (%.0f%% in the reader)",
  "at %s MiB, and %s GFF features %.1f s (%.0f%% in the reader) at %s MiB.\n\n"),
  format(short4$rows, big.mark = ","), short4$median_seconds,
  format(round(short4$rows / short4$median_seconds), big.mark = ","), 100 * short4$scan_share,
  short4$median_rss_mib, round(chr1_length / 2^20),
  format(vcf4$rows, big.mark = ","), vcf4$median_seconds, 100 * vcf4$scan_share, vcf4$median_rss_mib,
  format(gff4$rows, big.mark = ","), gff4$median_seconds, 100 * gff4$scan_share, gff4$median_rss_mib))
long1 <- cell_of("bam_long_reads", 1L)
long4 <- cell_of("bam_long_reads", 4L)
stopifnot(long4$row_groups == 1L)
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "Memory grows with the width of a row. In the builders' layout each sample of a VCF is one column,",
  "and a row group holds the genotypes of every sample for its records: on one thread %s samples take",
  "%s MiB peak RSS and %s samples %s MiB, about %.1f MiB per sample, for an input file of %s MiB and an",
  "output of %s MiB. Long reads make wide rows too: at 4× the ONT reads make one row group of %s rows,",
  "and the peak RSS is %s MiB, %s times the 1× peak.\n\n"),
  format(sample_counts[[1L]], big.mark = ","), samples_low$median_rss_mib,
  format(sample_counts[[3L]], big.mark = ","), samples_high$median_rss_mib, mib_per_sample,
  round(file.size(phase3_vcf) / 2^20, 1), samples_high$output_mib,
  format(long4$rows, big.mark = ","), long4$median_rss_mib,
  format(round(long4$median_rss_mib / long1$median_rss_mib, 2), nsmall = 2)))
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "The operating scale this report supports is what it measures: %s alignments of one 30× chromosome,",
  "a %ssingle-sample VCF of %s records, four copies of a full human annotation (%s features)",
  "and %s samples of %s records, all with the default row group of 100,000 rows. More samples, wider",
  "rows or a larger row group need memory in proportion; `row_group_size` is the builders' parameter",
  "for it, and its effect is not measured here.\n"),
  format(short4$rows, big.mark = ","), if (any(giab_fractions == 1)) "whole-genome " else "",
  format(vcf4$rows, big.mark = ","), format(gff4$rows, big.mark = ","),
  format(sample_counts[[3L]], big.mark = ","), format(phase3_records, big.mark = ",")))
```
